facts.label: reported
facts.quote: How much does your life insurance distributor earn from first-year endowment plan premiums? As much as 60%.
facts.text: Life insurance distributors can earn up to 60 percent of a customer's first-year premium in commission on traditional endowment plans.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: In life insurance, the 61st month persistency rate is only 48%, indicating that more than half of policyholders discontinue their policies before completing five years despite heavily front-loaded remuneration.
facts.text: The 61st month persistency rate across Indian life insurance stands at only 48 percent, meaning more than half of policyholders forfeit or lapse their policies before completing five years.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: The paper said distributor remuneration in the life insurance corporate agency channel grew 125% between FY23 and FY25, compared with a 28% rise in new business premium.
facts.text: Payments made to distributors in the life insurance corporate agency channel jumped 125 percent between FY23 and FY25, far outpacing the 28 percent growth in new business premiums.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: For life insurance policies with a term of 10 years and above, the first-year commission for agents is capped at 25%, followed by 5% in renewal commissions.
facts.text: IRDAI proposed capping the first-year agent commission on life policies with a term of 10 years and above at 25 percent.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: The commission will be 5.5% for renewals in the sixth, seventh and eighth policy years, 6% for the ninth, 10th and 11th years and so on, subject to a maximum renewal commission of 7%.
facts.text: Under the proposed commission overhaul, annual renewal commission paid to agents can gradually increase over the life of the policy up to a maximum cap of 7 percent to incentivize long-term persistency.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Firstly, IRDAI has extended the 'Free Look Period' in life insurance policies from 15 days to 30 days leading to an increased censure of flexibility to the consumers and policyholders to review and evaluate the terms and conditions of their policies.
facts.text: IRDAI doubled the mandatory free-look cancellation period from 15 days to 30 days, enabling households to review policy terms and obtain a complete refund if mis-sold.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: The Irdai master circular states: “the special surrender value (SSV) calculated shall become payable after completion of the first policy year provided one full year premium has been received.”
facts.text: Under the revised life product guidelines, a special surrender value becomes payable after the completion of just 1 policy year if the full annual premium was paid.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: If you surrender your policy during the second year of the policy, you will receive a total of 30% of the total premiums paid.
facts.text: Policyholders who surrender a regular non-single premium endowment plan during the second year are entitled to a guaranteed surrender value floor of 30 percent of total premiums paid.
